## Setup
```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Find the digitalrodent folder
root = Path.cwd().parent
print(root)

# Define paths for the MetaData, dual regression, combined dataset, and figures directories

meta_dir = root / "data" / "MetaData"
dr_dir = root / "results" / "dual_regression"
out_dir = root / "results" / "combined_dataset"
fig_dir = root / "results" / "figures"

out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
fig_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# Master list of the 15 datasets
datasets = pd.read_csv(root / "data" / "datasets.tsv", sep="\t", dtype=str)
datasets["Dataset_id"] = datasets["Dataset_id"].str.zfill(2)

display(datasets.fillna("NA"))
MM = 1 / 25.4

plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "Arial",
    "font.size": 6,
    "axes.labelsize": 8,
    "axes.titlesize": 8,
    "xtick.labelsize": 6,
    "ytick.labelsize": 6,
    "legend.fontsize": 6,
    "legend.title_fontsize": 6
})
```

Remove excluded subjects from the combined dataset and save the cleaned dataset to a new CSV file.
```{python}
exclude = pd.read_csv(root / "data" / "Exclude.tsv", sep="\t")

matches = []

# Loop through the excluded subjects and find matches in the combined dataset
for _, row in exclude.iterrows():

    subject = str(row["Subject"])
    dataset = str(row["Dataset"])
    session = None

    if dataset in ["Awake", "Awake_Rest"]:

        session = subject.split("_ses-")[1].split("_")[0]
        subject = subject.split("_")[0].replace("sub-", "").lstrip("0")

        subject_match = Combined_dataset[
            (Combined_dataset["Dataset_name"] == dataset) &
            (
                Combined_dataset["Participant_Id"]
                .astype(str)
                .str.replace("sub-", "", regex=False)
                .str.split("_ses-")
                .str[0]
                .str.lstrip("0")
                == subject
            ) &
            (
                Combined_dataset["Session"]
                .astype(str)
                .str.replace(".0", "", regex=False)
                == session
            )
        ]

    if subject_match.empty:
        print("NOT FOUND:", row["Subject"], dataset)
    else:
        print("FOUND:", row["Subject"], dataset)
        matches.append(subject_match)

excluded_matches = pd.concat(matches, ignore_index=True)

print(excluded_matches)

# Remove the excluded subjects from the combined dataset
print("Excluded shape:", excluded_matches.shape)
print("Combined before:", Combined_dataset.shape)

old_shape = Combined_dataset.shape

for _, row in excluded_matches.iterrows():
    Combined_dataset = Combined_dataset[
        ~(
            (Combined_dataset["Dataset_name"] == row["Dataset_name"]) &
            (Combined_dataset["Participant_Id"] == row["Participant_Id"]) &
            (Combined_dataset["Session"] == row["Session"])
        )
    ]

Combined_dataset = Combined_dataset.reset_index(drop=True)

new_shape = Combined_dataset.shape

print("Combined after:", new_shape)
print("Difference:", old_shape[0] - new_shape[0], "rows removed")

#TEMP EXCLUDE AWAKE MESSING THINGS UP
Combined_dataset = Combined_dataset[Combined_dataset["Dataset_name"] != "Awake"]

Combined_dataset["Anesthesia"] = Combined_dataset["Anesthesia"].str.lower()

Combined_dataset = Combined_dataset.fillna(np.nan)

Combined_dataset.to_csv(out_dir / "Combined_dataset.csv", index=False)

```

The following code generates a horizontal bar plot showing the number of scans per dataset, broken down by sex (F, M, NA). The x-axis is on a logarithmic scale to accommodate datasets with varying numbers of scans.
```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

gender_counts = (
    Combined_dataset
    .assign(Sex=Combined_dataset["Sex"].fillna("NA"))
    .groupby(["Dataset_name", "Sex"])
    .size()
    .unstack(fill_value=0)
)

gender_counts = gender_counts.loc[
    gender_counts.sum(axis=1).sort_values().index
]

print(gender_counts)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(180 * MM, 100 * MM))

left = [0] * len(gender_counts)

for sex, color in [("F", "sandybrown"), ("M", "steelblue"), ("NA", "gray")]:
    if sex in gender_counts.columns:
        ax.barh(
            gender_counts.index,
            gender_counts[sex],
            left=left,
            label=sex,
            color=color
        )

        left = left + gender_counts[sex].values

ax.set_xscale("log")
ax.set_xlabel("Number of scans")
ax.set_ylabel("Dataset")
ax.set_title("Number of scans per dataset")

ax.legend(title="Sex")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(root / "results" / "figures" / "scans_per_dataset.svg", format="svg", bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()


```

The following code generates a kernel density estimate (KDE) plot to visualize the age distribution of all scans in the combined dataset. 
```{python}
age = Combined_dataset["Age(week)"].dropna()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(180 * MM, 100 * MM))

age.plot(kind="kde", ax=ax, color="steelblue", linewidth=3)

ax.set_xlim(left=0)
```

The following code computes the mean age per dataset. It also generates a summary table showing the count, mean, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum age for each dataset.
```{python}
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", None)

print(
    Combined_dataset[
        ["Dataset_name", "Participant_Id", "Age(week)"]
    ]
    .sort_values("Age(week)", ascending=False)
)

print("\nMean age per dataset:")
print(
    Combined_dataset
    .groupby("Dataset_name")["Age(week)"]
    .mean()
    .sort_values(ascending=False)
)

age_table = (
    Combined_dataset
    .groupby("Dataset_name")["Age(week)"]
    .agg(["count", "mean", "std", "min", "max"])
    .round(2)
    .sort_values("mean", ascending=False)
)

print(age_table)
```

This code generates a heatmap to visualize the mean component values for each dataset. To see which datasets may have generally higher or lower values.
```{python}
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap

components = [f"comp{i}" for i in range(1, 19)]

Combined_dataset[components] = Combined_dataset[components].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")

heatmap_data = (
    Combined_dataset
    .groupby("Dataset_name")[components]
    .mean()
)

cmap = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
    "steelblue_sandybrown",
    ["steelblue", "lightblue", "wheat", "sandybrown"]
)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(180 * MM, 100 * MM))

im = ax.imshow(heatmap_data.values, aspect="auto", cmap=cmap)

ax.set_xticks(range(len(components)))
ax.set_xticklabels(components, rotation=45, ha="right")

ax.set_yticks(range(len(heatmap_data.index)))
ax.set_yticklabels(heatmap_data.index)

ax.set_xlabel("Component")
ax.set_ylabel("Dataset")
ax.set_title("Mean component value per dataset")

cbar = plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
cbar.set_label("Mean value")

plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig(
    root / "results" / "figures" / "component_heatmap.svg",
    format="svg",
    bbox_inches="tight"
)

plt.show()
```



Create a heatmap of standardized component values (Z-scores) for each dataset. This allows for comparison of component patterns across datasets, highlighting which datasets have higher or lower values relative to their own mean and standard deviation.
```{python}
components = [f"comp{i}" for i in range(1, 19)]

Combined_dataset[components] = Combined_dataset[components].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")

heatmap_data = (
    Combined_dataset
    .groupby("Dataset_name")[components]
    .median()
)

heatmap_z = heatmap_data.sub(
    heatmap_data.mean(axis=1),
    axis=0
)

heatmap_z = heatmap_z.div(
    heatmap_data.std(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan),
    axis=0
)

cmap = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
    "custom",
    ["steelblue", "lightblue", "wheat", "sandybrown"]
)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(180 * MM, 100 * MM))

im = ax.imshow(
    heatmap_z.values,
    aspect="auto",
    cmap=cmap
)

ax.set_xticks(range(len(components)))
ax.set_xticklabels(components, rotation=45, ha="right")

ax.set_yticks(range(len(heatmap_z.index)))
ax.set_yticklabels(heatmap_z.index)

ax.set_xlabel("Component")
ax.set_ylabel("Dataset")
ax.set_title("Standardized component pattern per dataset")

cbar = plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
cbar.set_label("Z-score")

plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig(
    root / "results" / "figures" / "component_heatmap_zscore.svg",
    format="svg",
    bbox_inches="tight"
)

plt.show()
```

Ridgeline plots for each component across datasets.
```{python}
from scipy.stats import gaussian_kde

components = [f"comp{i}" for i in range(1, 19)]

#Possibility to isolate a specific dataset
plot_data = Combined_dataset#[Combined_dataset["Dataset_name"] != "Alvino"]

for component in components:
    means = (
        plot_data
        .groupby("Dataset_name")[component]
        .mean()
        .sort_values(ascending=False)
    )

    datasets = means.index

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(180 * MM, 120 * MM))

    x_min = plot_data[component].min()
    x_max = plot_data[component].max()

    for i, dataset in enumerate(datasets):

        values = (
            plot_data.loc[
                plot_data["Dataset_name"] == dataset,
                component
            ]
            .dropna()
            .astype(float)
        )

        if len(values) < 2:
            continue

        x = np.linspace(x_min, x_max, 300)

        kde = gaussian_kde(values)
        density = kde(x)

        if density.max() == 0:
            continue

        density = density / density.max() * 0.8

        color = "steelblue" if i % 2 == 0 else "sandybrown"

        ax.fill_between(
            x,
            i,
            i + density,
            color=color,
            alpha=0.6
        )

        ax.plot(
            x,
            i + density,
            color=color
        )

        ax.hlines(
            y=i,
            xmin=x.min(),
            xmax=x.max(),
            color=color,
            linewidth=1
        )

        mean_val = values.mean()
        mean_height = np.interp(mean_val, x, density)

        ax.vlines(
            x=mean_val,
            ymin=i,
            ymax=i + mean_height,
            color="black",
            linewidth=1.5
        )

        low_vals = np.sort(values)[:2]
        high_vals = np.sort(values)[-2:]
        extreme_vals = np.concatenate([low_vals, high_vals])

        extreme_heights = np.interp(extreme_vals, x, density)

        ax.scatter(
            values,
            [i] * len(values),
            color="black",
            s=10,
            alpha=0.25,
            zorder=3
        )

    ax.set_yticks(range(len(datasets)))
    ax.set_yticklabels(datasets)

    ax.set_xlabel("DR value")
    ax.set_ylabel("Dataset")
    ax.set_title(component)

    plt.tight_layout()

    plt.savefig(
        root / "results" / "figures" / f"ridgeline_{component}.svg",
        format="svg",
        bbox_inches="tight"
    )

    plt.show()
```


Following code does everything that has already been done for the datasets for the normative model for the Alzheimer dataset.
## Alzheimer 
```{python}
Alzheimer = pd.read_csv(
    root / "data" / "Alzheimer" / "Alzheimer_MetaData.tsv",
    sep="\t"
)

components = [f"comp{i}" for i in range(18, 0, -1) if f"comp{i}" in Alzheimer.columns]

Alzheimer[components] = Alzheimer[components].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")

cmap = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
    "custom",
    ["steelblue", "lightblue", "white", "wheat", "sandybrown"]
)
# Heatmap
heatmap_data = Alzheimer[components].median().to_frame().T

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(180 * MM, 30 * MM))

im = ax.imshow(
    heatmap_data.values,
    aspect="auto",
    cmap=cmap
)

ax.set_xticks(range(len(components)))
ax.set_xticklabels(components, rotation=45, ha="right")

ax.set_yticks([0])
ax.set_yticklabels(["Alzheimer"])

ax.set_xlabel("Component")
ax.set_title("Median DR values")

cbar = plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, aspect=2)
cbar.set_label("Median DR value")

plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig(
    root / "results" / "figures" / "Alzheimer_component_heatmap.svg",
    format="svg",
    bbox_inches="tight"
)

plt.show()


# Ridgeline switched components to an axis
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(180 * MM, 120 * MM))

all_values = Alzheimer[components].values.flatten()
all_values = all_values[~np.isnan(all_values)]

x_min = all_values.min()
x_max = all_values.max()

for i, component in enumerate(components):

    values = Alzheimer[component].dropna().astype(float)

    if len(values) < 2:
        continue

    x = np.linspace(x_min, x_max, 300)

    kde = gaussian_kde(values)
    density = kde(x)
    density = density / density.max() * 0.8

    color = "steelblue" if i % 2 == 0 else "sandybrown"

    ax.fill_between(
        x,
        i,
        i + density,
        color=color,
        alpha=0.6
    )

    ax.plot(
        x,
        i + density,
        color=color
    )

    ax.hlines(
        y=i,
        xmin=x.min(),
        xmax=x.max(),
        color=color,
        linewidth=1
    )

    mean_val = values.mean()
    mean_height = np.interp(mean_val, x, density)

    ax.vlines(
        x=mean_val,
        ymin=i,
        ymax=i + mean_height,
        color="black",
        linewidth=1.5
    )

    ax.scatter(
        values,
        [i] * len(values),
        color="black",
        s=10,
        alpha=0.25,
        zorder=3
    )

ax.set_yticks(range(len(components)))
ax.set_yticklabels(components)

ax.set_xlabel("DR value")
ax.set_ylabel("Component")
ax.set_title("Alzheimer component distributions")

plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig(
    root / "results" / "figures" / "Alzheimer_ridgeline_components.svg",
```
